# older than 30 days, judged from the PARSED DATE (so a repo
# reviewed yesterday but dated last month is still flagged).

findings.comment: Contract contradiction: the header comment says staleness is 'judged from the PARSED DATE' (the 'Last reviewed:' date inside ROADMAP.md), but the code checks the file's modification time (`find -mtime -30`). A repo whose ROADMAP was touched yesterday but whose 'Last reviewed:' date is months old will be reported OK, defeating the stated purpose of the anti-rot guard. The check must parse the date from the file content instead.

evidence.quote:
# older than 30 days, judged from the PARSED DATE (so a repo
# reviewed yesterday but dated last month is still flagged).

good: Script uses `set -euo pipefail` and handles missing ROADMAP.md gracefully by skipping the repo.
Accepts multiple repos as arguments and reports a per-repo OK/STALE status, which is easy to consume in CI.
expected_result.summary: The script's own comment promises the freshness check is 'judged from the PARSED DATE' in ROADMAP.md, but the implementation uses the file's modification time via `find -mtime -30`. Any edit to the file (even one that leaves the 'Last reviewed:' date stale) resets mtime and suppresses the flag, so the guard does not do what it claims.

notes: Right bug, right kind and harm, but the quote contains only the contract ('judged from the PARSED DATE'), not the -mtime -30 implementation that creates the contradiction.
